package main

// Generated into the module under test by TestGRPCOnlyJWTEndpoints.
// __MODULE__ is replaced with the generated module path.

import (
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5"
	"go.uber.org/config"

	jwtserver "__MODULE__/auth/jwtserver"
	"__MODULE__/info"
)

const testKey = "test-signing-key"

// newServer returns the JWT server, built once. It is a singleton because
// jwtserver.New registers its routes on the GLOBAL http.DefaultServeMux, and
// Go's mux panics on a duplicate pattern — so it can only be constructed once
// per process.
//
// Core is nil: every assertion below is on a path that fails before the database
// is reached, so no DB is needed.
var newServer = sync.OnceValues(func() (jwtserver.Interface, error) {
	provider, err := config.NewYAML(config.Source(strings.NewReader("auth:\n  jwt:\n    key: " + testKey + "\n")))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	impl, err := jwtserver.New(jwtserver.Params{Config: provider})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return impl.(jwtserver.Interface), nil
})

func mustServer(t *testing.T) jwtserver.Interface {
	t.Helper()
	s, err := newServer()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return s
}

// TestAuthRoutesMounted is the direct regression test for the misdiagnosis that
// prompted this work: on a REST-less (gRPC-only) build the JWT endpoints must
// resolve to their OWN mux patterns. If they fell through to the info page's "/"
// catch-all they would 404, which is exactly what made the auth surface look
// absent.
func TestAuthRoutesMounted(t *testing.T) {
	info.Register()
	mustServer(t)

	for _, p := range []string{"/signin", "/refresh", "/validate"} {
		_, pattern := http.DefaultServeMux.Handler(httptest.NewRequest("POST", p, nil))
		if pattern != p {
			t.Errorf("%s resolved to mux pattern %q, want %q — the auth endpoint is not mounted (%q means it fell through to the info page catch-all)", p, pattern, p, "/")
		}
	}
}

func TestSignInMethodNotAllowed(t *testing.T) {
	s := mustServer(t)

	// A bare GET used to reach the body decode and answer 400, which reads as
	// "bad credentials" rather than "wrong method".
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	s.SignIn(rec, httptest.NewRequest("GET", "/signin", nil))
	if rec.Code != http.StatusMethodNotAllowed {
		t.Errorf("GET /signin = %d, want %d", rec.Code, http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
	}
	if allow := rec.Header().Get("Allow"); !strings.Contains(allow, "POST") {
		t.Errorf("GET /signin Allow header = %q, want it to list POST", allow)
	}
	assertErrorBody(t, rec, "GET /signin")

	rec = httptest.NewRecorder()
	s.SignIn(rec, httptest.NewRequest("OPTIONS", "/signin", nil))
	if rec.Code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Errorf("OPTIONS /signin = %d, want %d", rec.Code, http.StatusOK)
	}
}

func TestSignInBadBody(t *testing.T) {
	s := mustServer(t)

	// Form encoding rather than JSON — one of the shapes tried against the live
	// deploy while diagnosing this.
	req := httptest.NewRequest("POST", "/signin", strings.NewReader("email=a@b.com&password=x"))
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	s.SignIn(rec, req)
	if rec.Code != http.StatusBadRequest {
		t.Errorf("POST /signin (form-encoded) = %d, want %d", rec.Code, http.StatusBadRequest)
	}
	assertErrorBody(t, rec, "POST /signin (form-encoded)")
}

// TestRefreshMalformedToken guards a nil-pointer panic: ParseWithClaims returns
// a NIL token for a string that does not split into three segments, and Refresh
// used to read tkn.Valid before checking err.
func TestRefreshMalformedToken(t *testing.T) {
	s := mustServer(t)

	for _, tok := range []string{"", "garbage", "a.b"} {
		rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
		body := strings.NewReader(fmt.Sprintf("{%q:%q}", "token", tok))
		func() {
			defer func() {
				if r := recover(); r != nil {
					t.Fatalf("POST /refresh with token %q panicked: %v", tok, r)
				}
			}()
			s.Refresh(rec, httptest.NewRequest("POST", "/refresh", body))
		}()
		if rec.Code != http.StatusUnauthorized {
			t.Errorf("POST /refresh with token %q = %d, want %d", tok, rec.Code, http.StatusUnauthorized)
		}
		assertErrorBody(t, rec, "POST /refresh with token "+tok)
	}
}

// TestValidateWithoutToken guards the 500-that-should-have-been-401.
func TestValidateWithoutToken(t *testing.T) {
	s := mustServer(t)

	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	s.Validate(rec, httptest.NewRequest("GET", "/validate", nil))
	if rec.Code != http.StatusUnauthorized {
		t.Errorf("GET /validate with no Authorization header = %d, want %d", rec.Code, http.StatusUnauthorized)
	}
	assertErrorBody(t, rec, "GET /validate")
}

// TestTokenWireFormat guards the golang-jwt v5 migration. A token minted the way
// SignIn mints one must parse, and `exp` must still serialise as a plain integer
// — that is what keeps tokens issued by the previous jwt-go v3 build valid.
func TestTokenWireFormat(t *testing.T) {
	s := mustServer(t)

	exp := time.Now().Add(time.Hour).Truncate(time.Second)
	tokenString, err := jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodHS256, &jwtserver.Claims{
		Email:            "a@b.com",
		RegisteredClaims: jwt.RegisteredClaims{ExpiresAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(exp)},
	}).SignedString([]byte(testKey))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	parser, ok := s.(interface {
		ParseToken(string) (*jwtserver.Claims, error)
	})
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("jwtserver implementation does not expose ParseToken(string)")
	}
	claims, err := parser.ParseToken(tokenString)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ParseToken rejected a freshly minted token: %v", err)
	}
	if claims.Email != "a@b.com" {
		t.Errorf("email claim = %q, want %q", claims.Email, "a@b.com")
	}
	if claims.ExpiresAt == nil || !claims.ExpiresAt.Time.Equal(exp) {
		t.Errorf("exp claim = %v, want %v", claims.ExpiresAt, exp)
	}

	raw, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(strings.Split(tokenString, ".")[1])
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var payload map[string]any
	dec := json.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(string(raw)))
	dec.UseNumber()
	if err := dec.Decode(&payload); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	got, ok := payload["exp"].(json.Number)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("exp claim is %T, want a JSON number", payload["exp"])
	}
	if strings.ContainsAny(got.String(), ".eE") {
		t.Errorf("exp serialised as %q, want a plain integer — v3-issued tokens would stop validating", got.String())
	}
}

// TestSigningMethodPinned checks that parsing refuses an algorithm SignIn never
// mints, rather than letting the token's own header pick the verifier.
func TestSigningMethodPinned(t *testing.T) {
	s := mustServer(t)

	parser, ok := s.(interface {
		ParseToken(string) (*jwtserver.Claims, error)
	})
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("jwtserver implementation does not expose ParseToken(string)")
	}

	header := base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(`{"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"}`))
	body := base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(`{"email":"attacker@example.com"}`))
	if _, err := parser.ParseToken(header + "." + body + "."); err == nil {
		t.Error("ParseToken accepted an alg=none token")
	}
}

func assertErrorBody(t *testing.T, rec *httptest.ResponseRecorder, what string) {
	t.Helper()
	var body struct {
		Error string `json:"error"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &body); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("%s: body %q is not JSON (%v) — a bodiless failure is indistinguishable from the mux's own 404", what, rec.Body.String(), err)
		return
	}
	if body.Error == "" {
		t.Errorf("%s: response carries no error message", what)
	}
}
